name: Milady's
take: The old Soho dive came back as a proper cocktail bar with a marble counter, and it kept the loose, loud, anyone-welcome feel.
theCatch: Tables can be booked; the bar is walk-in and fills by 8 on weekends.
notes: Reopened October 2022 by Julie Reiner (Clover Club, Leyenda) in the corner space of the original Milady's, which closed in 2014. Cocktails around $20 with a half-size 'cheeky' pour option; menu splits into dive and high-dive sections (burger, crab mac and cheese, corn dog poppers). Closes at midnight most nights, 2am Fri-Sat.

name: Pearl Box
take: Red carpet up the stairs, velvet loveseats, martinis and caviar: the dressed-up Soho night for when the group wants to feel expensive.
theCatch: Book on Resy for a weekend; it closes by midnight, so this is the first stop, not the last.
notes: Opened fall 2024 above the Heroes restaurant at 357 W Broadway, spread over three floors (Salon, Parlor, Attic). Martinis, champagne, caviar service, and a $14 candy-bowl dessert built for photos. Tue-Thu 5:30-11:30pm, Fri-Sat to midnight, Sun to 10pm; walk-ins accepted but reservations recommended.

name: South Soho Bar
take: Dark, booth-lined, and small enough to feel like a secret, with classic cocktails done straight and chicken nuggets that are better than they need to be.
theCatch: Maybe a dozen seats; reserve for a weekend or come before 8 and take a booth.
notes: Sister bar to The Tyger next door, with a discreet entrance on Centre St just north of Canal. Small dark room with a long bar, a few booths, and a sliding ladder along the back-bar liquor wall. Riffs on classics (daiquiris, old fashioneds) plus snacks like chicken nuggets, grilled cheese and crudo. Open to 1am nightly (from 4pm weekdays, 2pm weekends); reservations recommended on weekends.

name: Beyond The Pale
take: An Irish pub that went to finishing school: Guinness and wings up front, candlelit tables and an olive-oil martini in the back.
theCatch: Happy hour runs weekdays 4:30-6:30, and the back room is the calmer seat.
notes: Long dark room between Lafayette and Mulberry with a wooden bar, leather booths, big communal tables and a candlelit seating area in back; no TVs. Cocktails (Oaxacan old fashioned, an olive-oil vodka martini), Guinness, wings and Parmesan fries. Hours run to midnight Mon/Sun, 1am Tue, 2am Wed, 3am Thu-Sat. Reservations by email; happy hour Mon-Fri 4:30-6:30pm.

name: Mother's Ruin
take: The Nolita bar everyone ends up at: real cocktails, a frozen of the day, and a burger at 3am, with nobody at the door checking your shoes.
theCatch: No reservations and only a few tables; after 9 on weekends you're standing.
notes: Open daily 11am-4am with the kitchen running until 3:30am (burger, fried chicken sandwich, wings, French onion grilled cheese) and brunch until 4pm. Signature cocktails $16-17, a rotating frozen 'Slushy du Jour', beer $6-8, wine $12. No reservations and no door policy; narrow exposed-brick room with a long bar, a few tables, and some big wooden tables that groups grab.

name: Botanica Bar
address: 47 E Houston St, New York, NY 10012
take: Thrift-store couches, cheap well drinks, a DJ on weekends, and a back room that fills with people who came for the price and stayed for the dark.
theCatch: Happy hour runs until 7 every day; no kitchen, so bring your own slice.
notes: Below-street lounge on the south side of Houston between Mulberry and Mott. Hours Sun-Wed 5pm-1am, Thu 5pm-2am, Fri 5pm-3am, Sat 4pm-3am. Happy hour daily until 7pm: $6 wells and house wine, $2 off drafts, $3 off frozens. Kitchen is permanently closed and outside food is allowed; the back room is reservable for groups of 30-45; DJs on weekends.

name: Milano's Bar
address: 51 E Houston St, New York, NY 10012
take: A narrow cash-only dive that opens at 8am and has looked the same since before Nolita had a name; cheap beer, a loud jukebox, no food.
theCatch: Cash only, no kitchen, and only a handful of stools in back; don't bring more than four.
notes: Long, narrow bar between Mott and Mulberry on the south side of Houston, open Mon-Sat 8am-4am and Sun from 10am. Cash only, beer and shots, no kitchen, walls of old photos. Same ownership group as d.b.a. and Doc Holliday's; reopened June 2021 after a 15-month pandemic closure. Some listings mention live jazz on Monday afternoons.

name: Toad Hall
take: A real neighborhood bar on Grand Street with a pool table, cheap pints, and regulars who've been on the same stools for years; open till 4 every night.
theCatch: No kitchen, so order delivery to the bar; the pool table has a wait after 9.
notes: Between West Broadway and Wooster, open daily noon-4am. Draft beer, a pool table, TVs for games, exposed brick and red stools. No food; regulars order takeout to the bar. Recent reviews are mostly warm about the bartenders, with the occasional complaint about surly service.

name: La Compagnie des Vins Surnaturels
take: A French wine bar with a bottle list the size of a novel, staff who'll steer you, and low couches for a date that goes long.
theCatch: Happy hour ends at 6 on weekdays and 4 on weekends; after that the glasses get pricey.
notes: Experimental Group's New York outpost of the Paris wine bar, on Centre St between Grand and Broome; about 70 seats. Roughly 25 wines by the glass plus hundreds of bottles, mostly French and natural-leaning, with charcuterie and light bites. Happy hour ($5 snacks, $5 off glasses) until 6pm weekdays and 4pm weekends. Bar seats, tables, and a semi-private room for groups.

name: Broome Street Bar
take: The corner pub Soho forgot to gentrify: a decent beer list, burgers on pita, and enough tables that eight of you can just sit down.
theCatch: Expect hotel tourists at dinner time; it's the burger-and-pint stop, not the cocktail stop.
notes: Corner of West Broadway and Broome, same owners for more than three decades; stained-glass window, chalkboard menus, microbrews on tap (Schneider Weisse and the like) and pub food including burgers served on pita. Open from 11am; roughly 1:30am close weeknights and 2am weekends. Draws hotel guests and neighborhood regulars; on The Infatuation's Soho/Nolita list as the big-group pick.

name: The Vig Bar
take: High-tops, blue leather booths, a back room for sixty, and a 4am close: the Nolita bar for a birthday that starts as drinks and becomes a night.
theCatch: Email ahead to hold the back room; couples early, a singles crowd after 11.
notes: Corner of Spring and Elizabeth; open until 4am every night (from 5pm Mon-Tue, 3pm Wed-Thu, 2pm Fri-Sun). Dark Art Deco-leaning room with blue leather banquettes and high-tops; the back room fits 50-60 and gets booked for birthdays and office parties through events@vigbar.com. The site mentions live sports in the outdoor area. The Infatuation's guide files it as a pregame bar.

name: Local
take: A beer-and-wine bar on Sullivan with free popcorn, a dark window nook for two, and sidewalk seats for the nights you don't want a plan.
theCatch: Happy hour 4-6 daily comes with a free hot dog; beer and wine only, no martinis.
notes: Compact beer-and-wine bar between Prince and Houston with counter seats, a quieter back room with tables, a window nook, and a good amount of outdoor seating. Ciders and sours on the list; free popcorn on request. Happy hour daily 4-6pm with a complimentary hot dog or cheese and crackers. Its old localnyc.com domain is parked, so check Instagram for current hours.

name: Onieal's Grand Street
take: A Grand Street tavern since 1995 with a bootlegger tunnel for a wine cellar, cocktails, a real kitchen, and a 4am close on weekends.
theCatch: Kitchen runs until midnight; weekends it's a birthday-party room, so book if you're more than six.
notes: 174 Grand St between Lafayette and Mulberry; the venue site lists Mon-Wed to 2am, Thu to 3am, Fri-Sat to 4am, with an all-day tavern menu until midnight and weekend brunch. The building was a Prohibition-era speakeasy and gambling parlor and the old tunnel is now the wine cellar. Rotating East Coast craft beers, cocktails, and private-party bookings (birthdays, corporate, bottle brunches) are the draw.

name: JIMMY
take: Eighteen floors up with the Hudson on one side and Midtown on the other; the Soho rooftop that earns its cocktail prices on a clear night.
theCatch: Reserve on Resy for the roof deck in summer; dress a little, and don't show up in a big group unannounced.
notes: Rooftop bar atop the ModernHaus SoHo hotel (formerly The James) at Thompson and Grand, 18 floors up; open year-round, 5pm to midnight Sun-Tue, 1am Wed-Thu, 2am Fri-Sat. Indoor room with 14-foot windows and a fireplace conversation pit in winter; roof deck with a pool in summer. Reservations via Resy or email; the venue asks for 'upscale but casual' attire.

name: Balthazar
take: The big red brasserie that's been a scene since 1997, and still is: steak frites, a tower of shellfish, and a bar you can walk up to.
theCatch: Bar seats are walk-in before 7 or after 9; the dining room needs a Resy weeks out.
notes: Keith McNally's French brasserie at 80 Spring St, open daily from breakfast through late supper with weekend brunch; Michelin-recommended. Steak frites in the low $40s, bread basket $22; Resy reservations, with walk-in bar seating easiest before 7pm or after 9pm. Crowd mixes regulars, Soho shoppers and out-of-towners.

name: Raoul's
take: Dark, crowded, and unchanged since the seventies; get the bar, order the peppercorn burger before the twelve run out, then walk to Milady's.
theCatch: Only 12 burgers a night at the bar, first come; Resy opens 30 days out and goes fast.
notes: French bistro at 180 Prince St since 1975; dinner nightly (bar from 5pm, kitchen 5:15pm), brunch Sat-Sun 11-2:30. Reservations only via Resy, 30 days out, tables max 8. The burger au poivre is bar-only, 12 per night, first come. Oil paintings, a stag head, a fish tank between the front and back rooms; card payments must be chip and no Apple Pay.

name: Rubirosa
take: Thin vodka-sauce pizza, ravioli, and a room so packed it runs like a bar; the Nolita dinner that feeds eight people without anyone checking the bill twice.
theCatch: Resy releases weekly and vanishes; walk-ins wait an hour-plus on weekends, so put your name in and go to Spring Lounge.
notes: 235 Mulberry between Prince and Spring, open daily 11am-11pm. Family from Joe & Pat's on Staten Island; signature tie-dye pizza (vodka sauce and pesto), fresh pasta, a big gluten-free menu, house wine around $15 a glass. Reservations on Resy released weekly; walk-ins accepted with long weekend waits and a small outdoor shed.

name: Emilio's Ballato
address: 55 E Houston St, New York, NY 10012
take: No reservations, a front room of celebrity photos, a hidden back room, and veal that costs what it costs; old Houston Street Italian, worth the wait once.
theCatch: Walk-in only; a table for six on a Tuesday is half an hour, Saturday can run past two hours.
notes: 55 E Houston between Mott and Mulberry, family-run since 1956. Walk-in only, no reservations; front room lined with celebrity photos and a windowless back room used for groups. Southern Italian: bolognese, off-menu vitello antonio, chicken parm around $40, veal dishes up to $85, family-style portions add up. Time Out lists Mon-Fri noon-11pm, Sat 4pm-midnight, Sun 4-11pm; cards accepted.

name: La Esquina
take: Tacos at the corner counter, or through the kitchen and down to the brasserie for mezcal, dim light, and a room that runs until 2.
theCatch: Book the downstairs on OpenTable; the taqueria upstairs stays open until 5am for the after-bar taco.
notes: 114 Kenmare St at Lafayette: a street-level taqueria and takeout window, a casual cafe, and the underground brasserie entered through the kitchen. Time Out lists taqueria hours to 5am, cafe noon-midnight, restaurant 6pm-2am. Mains around $20-25; deep tequila and mezcal list sorted by region. Reservations through the venue site; $25 per person late-cancel fee; parties of 9+ handled separately.
